newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Record high rate boosts Bulgaria repo turnover.
newsitem.headline: Record high rate boosts Bulgaria repo turnover.

text.p: Only two corporate issues traded on the Bulgarian stock market this week as weekly repo turnover hit an all-time high on Friday due to a record high main interest rate, brokers said.

"Corporate stocks have been out of favour with brokers and investors for months because of their low liquidity and low yields compared to other investments such as treasury paper and foreign currency," said a broker.
Weekly repo turnover on local bourses rose to 23.619 million levs all-time high from 3.539 million levs the week before and a previous record high of 16.2 billion levs two months ago.

Treasury paper became an especially attractive investment after the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) raised its central interest rate to 300 percent annual from 108 percent, effective Tuesday, traders said.
One corporate issue traded unchanged from previous Friday's close and one fell.
Razvitie Investment Fund (RIF) third issue closed at 32 levs, down 5.88 percent from last week and below par of 100.
Total stock turnover amounted to 15,550 levs ($67) and traded volume was 400 stocks.

Bank shares were offered below par but there was no demand for them after the BNB on Monday put under special supervision nine local banks in a bid to stabilise the country's crumbling banking sector, brokers said.
Five other banks expect court rulings on insolvency suits filed against them by the BNB three months ago.
The 13-share Reuter All Bulgaria Stock Index (RABSI) closed at 41.02 points, down 0.12 from last Friday, due to the fall of RIF' third issue.
* RABSI calculated on daily basis since February 1, 1994 -- Dessislava Popova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
